findings.finding: The defining pairing eta(Phi(u),w)=F(u,w) and displayed Phi^mu=eta^{mu alpha}F_{alpha beta}u^beta have opposite signs under F_ab=F(e_a,e_b).
findings.witness: In the standard Minkowski frame take F_01=1, F_10=-1, all other coefficients zero and u=e_0. The defining pairing gives Phi(u)=e_1; the displayed coefficient formula gives -e_1.
findings.missing_obligation: Make the invariant pairing, coordinate formula and conditional force-equation convention agree without changing the orthogonality/norm-conservation claims. Review the symmetric F=eta boundary example and the future planned physical force consumer.

findings.finding: A strictly increasing C1 surjection may have phi'=0, so x composed with phi need not satisfy the definition of future timelike worldline. The strategy incorrectly treats a zero tangent as future timelike.
findings.witness: Take a straight future timelike x on [-1,1] and phi(u)=u^3 on [-1,1]. phi is an increasing C1 surjection and the composed tangent vanishes at zero.
findings.missing_obligation: Retain the broad elapsed-integral substitution result for monotone C1 maps, and distinguish the nonvanishing-derivative condition required for the composed curve to remain a worldline. Decreasing maps similarly may have zero tangent.

findings.finding: The hypotheses allow omega=0 but the conclusion asserts gamma^4 R^2 omega^4>0 and spacelike acceleration.
findings.witness: omega=0 satisfies R|omega|<c and produces a clock at rest with A=0.
findings.missing_obligation: Preserve the allowed omega range, state nonnegative squared acceleration and spacelike acceleration precisely when omega is nonzero. Preserve the nonzero numerical specialization.
